title: Style constraint
description: One enforceable rule of assembly on a style node. Ruling of 23 Aug 2026 (docs/open-questions.md #24): reuses the fault corpus's `test` object pattern (schema/fault.schema.json) rather than inventing a separate rule language, extended with a `one-of` direction for enumerable/categorical rules and a `scope` field so the validator, composer and geometry solver can each ask 'which of this style's hard constraints can I actually evaluate from what I have.' The human-readable `statement` is kept beside the `test` in every case -- the test is a formalisation of the statement, not a replacement (PLAN-OF-ACTION.md section 1, 'Prose constraints stay').

id.description: Stable, never reused. <style-id>.c01, c02, ... in the order the constraints appear on the node. If a constraint is later found wrong, add a corrected one with a new id and mark this one deprecated_in_favour_of -- do not renumber or delete.

kind.description: Unchanged from the pre-existing constraint shape.

severity.description: Unchanged from the pre-existing constraint shape.

statement.description: The human-readable rule, verbatim. Never edited to fit a test -- if the test can only formalise part of the statement, the test covers that part and the rest stays prose.

scope.description: What kind of record could supply the variables this constraint needs. 'judgment' means the sources do not determine this numerically -- decision not to undo #6, extended from slots to constraints: a judgment-scope constraint has no `test` and is listed for hand review, never silently passed or invented a threshold for.

deprecated_in_favour_of.description: Set only when this id has been superseded. The id itself is never reused or deleted.

test.description: Present only when scope is not 'judgment' and the statement itself supplies a number or an enumerable set. Absent (not empty) otherwise -- absence is not a formalisation failure to hide, it is the honest state.

expression.description: References one or more named variables from build/constraint_vocabulary.py. e.g. 'bay_count' or 'facade_width_ft / facade_height_ft'.

direction.description: The condition for the constraint being SATISFIED (unlike the fault schema, where the test object describes when a fault is PRESENT -- inverted here because a constraint states what must be true, a fault states what must not be). 'between' uses threshold as the lower bound and `upper` as the upper bound. 'one-of' uses `set` instead of `threshold`.

threshold.description: Required for at-least / at-most / equals / between (as the lower bound). Omitted for one-of.

set.description: The permitted values when direction is 'one-of'. e.g. ["3", "5", "7"] for an odd-bay-count rule, or a set of enum ids for a categorical slot value.

units.description: Free-form but should match a unit already in use elsewhere in the corpus (in, ft, deg, rise_in_12, count, ratio, percent, courses) unless the vocabulary variable's own unit makes this redundant.

measurable_from.description: Named the same as the fault schema's field of the same purpose, deliberately -- what a model or a person looking at this kind of record could actually evaluate the expression from. Independent of `scope`: scope says what KIND of record supplies the variables in principle; measurable_from says what's needed to actually read them off in practice (a plan-scope constraint might still only be readable from a rendered elevation, not the raw room list).
